about.title: Type faster. Stress less.
about.intro: Millions of people type every single day - emails, messages, documents, code. But most never learned to do it properly. They look at the keyboard, use a few fingers, and it works. Sort of.
about.missionText: Touch typists are 40-60% faster than self-taught typists. That's not a motivational quote, that's data. The skill gap is real - and the tools to close it are long overdue.
about.missionText2: We built Fast Forward >> Typing because there was no tool that truly fit. Not a school program. Not a kids game. Not a speed test with no structure. A modern course for adults who spend their days at a computer and simply want to get better at it.
about.howText: A free typing test shows you where you stand. A structured course, 15 minutes a day, teaches you touch typing from scratch. A certificate proves you did it.
about.howText2: No subscription. No account required to start. No guilt trips when you skip a day.
about.languagesText: German, English, French - not translated, but natively written for each language. Because "du" is not "you" is not "tu".
about.ctaText: Start with the free typing test. Takes less than 5 minutes.

hero.title: Your team thinks fast. Does it type that fast?
hero.subtitle: Emails, tickets, docs, AI prompts: your team writes all day. With touch typing, every person saves over two hours of it. Every day.
hero.fact: Here's the thing: companies spend five figures on AI tools. The biggest lever gets overlooked: how fast the team gets its thoughts into the keyboard.

why.title: The simplest productivity boost for your whole team
why.intro: Until the 90s, typing speed was on the certificate. Today every company assumes it and none of them measures it. Four reasons why.

items.title: It was considered solved
items.desc: The assumption: anyone who works at a computer all day can type. The average today is 40 words per minute, and half of that is hunting with two to four fingers.

items.title: It is invisible
items.desc: Slow typing produces no errors anyone notices. It just makes everything written a third slower.

items.title: It feels trivial
items.desc: A typing test in a job interview feels like a 1985 secretarial pool. So nobody asks, and nobody has to answer. The skill is assumed instead of checked.

items.title: The tools target the head
items.desc: AI assistants and dictation apps make thinking faster. In the end a human still types: prompts, corrections, emails, chat. AI did not abolish typing, it multiplied it.

why.closing: What nobody measures does not improve. That is why every team training with us starts with a measurement, and ends with one.
